newsitem.title: FINLAND: Washington stands firm on NATO expansion-Albright.
newsitem.headline: Washington stands firm on NATO expansion-Albright.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, arriving with President Bill Clinton for a summit with Russia, said on Thursday NATO's planned eastward expansion would go ahead despite Moscow's objections.
"I think they have to understand that we have a schedule that is going to go forward and that is the track that we are going to pursue," Albright told reporters travelling to Helsinki with Clinton.
Top U.S. officials told reporters they did not expect Russia, which bitterly opposes NATO expansion, to change its position but suggested an amicable solution was possible.
"We're going to disagree on NATO enlargement and I don't expect them to change their views and they shouldn't expect us to change our views," U.S. National Security Adviser Sandy Berger said.
"But on this issue we will agree to disagree," he added.
The NATO plan is to invite new members -- probably Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic -- to join the 16-member security alliance at a summit scheduled to be held in Madrid in July.
